name: Bronze-and-iron crossbow bolt
summary: A single Eastern Zhou crossbow bolt in the British Museum joins a leaded-bronze head to an iron shaft, probably by casting the bronze onto the iron.
description: CB3 combines a leaded-bronze head with the treated iron shaft.
tier_reason: Demote this specimen-level composite; reject merging away its distinct material/assembly contribution. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: by c. 301 BCE (museum attribution)
date.basis: CB3 is museum-attributed to the fifth–fourth centuries BCE; the historical manufacture/use inference has no independently known earliest bound and the findspot is unrecorded.

events.statement: A completed composite crossbow bolt with a bronze head and an iron shaft existed within the museum-attributed Eastern Zhou horizon.
events.population: The historical makers of the single CB3 composite object
events.caveats: The exact findspot and archaeological context are unrecorded; historical use as a weapon or dates of manufacture cannot be observed directly. The 2006 study is not the ancient use date. The makers are inferred from the finished object, and actual firing is not documented.

evidence.locator: p. 98 Table 1 CB3; pp. 99–100 object and metallographic analysis
evidence.supports: The same CB3 object, attributed 5th–4th century BCE, combines the head and the analyzed shaft.

date.label: 500–301 BCE
date.basis: Same CB3 attribution as its shaft; these are two production stages evidenced by one object.

events.statement: CB3 combines a leaded-bronze head with the treated iron shaft.
events.caveats: Casting-on is proposed, not directly observed in manufacture.
